title: Maintain basic safety, health and environmental issues

lessons.title: Hazards at work and your rights and duties
lessons.html:
Hazards at work

A hazard is anything that can hurt you, make you sick or damage the environment. A risk is how likely it is to happen and how bad it could be. At a grain silo or on a farm there are many hazards.

Hazards you will find

  • Moving machines: conveyors, augers, elevators, belts and tractors can catch clothes, hair and hands.
  • Vehicles: trucks reversing at the intake, forklifts.
  • Heights: ladders, silo roofs, walkways.
  • Dust: grain dust harms your lungs and can explode.
  • Noise: fans, dryers and hammer mills can damage your hearing.
  • Chemicals: fumigants and insecticides are poisons.
  • Heavy lifting: bags can hurt your back.
  • Confined spaces: bins and pits can trap you or have no fresh air.

Your rights and duties

The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says:

  • The employer must make the workplace as safe as reasonably possible, train workers and give them the right PPE.
  • The worker must work safely, obey the safety rules, wear PPE, and report unsafe conditions and injuries.

You may refuse to do work that is clearly dangerous. Explain why to your supervisor and report it. Most sites have a health and safety representative. Know who that person is. You can go to them with safety worries. They will help you raise the problem with management.

Safety signs

Colour and shapeMeaning
Red circle with a lineNot allowed, for example no smoking
Blue circleMust do, for example wear ear protection
Yellow triangleWarning, danger
Green squareSafe way, emergency exit, first aid

lessons.title: Working safely every day
lessons.html:
Working safely every day

Wear your PPE

  • Safety boots on all work areas.
  • Dust mask in dusty areas.
  • Ear plugs or muffs where the blue sign says so.
  • Gloves when handling bags, wire or chemicals.
  • Reflective vest near trucks.
  • Harness when working at heights, if trained.

Check your PPE before use. Report damaged PPE and ask for new.

Machines

  • Never remove guards from machines.
  • Never reach into a running machine.
  • Before cleaning or fixing a machine, it must be switched off and locked out. Only authorised people may do lock-out.
  • No loose clothes, jewellery or long loose hair near moving parts.
  • Know where the emergency stop is.

Lifting

  1. Check the weight first.
  2. Stand close to the load, feet apart.
  3. Bend your knees, keep your back straight.
  4. Lift with your legs.
  5. Do not twist while carrying. Turn with your feet.
  6. Get help or a trolley for heavy loads.

Housekeeping

  • Sweep up spilt grain and dust. Dust is a fire and explosion danger.
  • Keep walkways and exits clear.
  • Put tools away after use.
  • No smoking except in the marked smoking area.

Vehicles and trucks

  • Wear your reflective vest near the weighbridge and intake.
  • Walk only on marked walkways.
  • Never walk behind a reversing truck.
  • Make eye contact with the driver before you cross in front of a truck.

Look after your health

  • Drink water, especially on hot days.
  • Wash your hands before eating.
  • Report coughing, rashes or hearing problems to the clinic.
  • Rest when you feel dizzy or sick, and tell your supervisor.

lessons.title: Caring for the environment and reporting
lessons.html:
Caring for the environment

The environment is the land, water, air, plants and animals around us. Our work can harm it if we are careless. The National Water Act 36 of 1998 protects water resources, and pollution of rivers and groundwater is against the law.

What you can do

  • Waste: put waste in the right bins. Keep paper, plastic, metal and oily waste apart. Never burn plastic or dump waste in the veld.
  • Oil and fuel: catch drips with a drip tray. Clean spills with the spill kit. Keep oil out of drains.
  • Chemicals: never wash chemical containers in a river or dam. Return empty containers as your site says.
  • Dust: keep dust down by cleaning and closing covers on conveyors.
  • Water and power: close taps, report leaks, switch off lights and machines that are not in use.
  • Spilt grain: it feeds rats and pigeons. Clean it up.

Reporting

Report to your supervisor straight away:

  • Any injury, even small.
  • Any near miss: something that almost hurt someone.
  • Unsafe conditions: a broken guard, a damaged ladder, a missing grid.
  • Unsafe acts: someone working without PPE or reaching into a machine.
  • Spills and leaks.

Reporting is not telling tales. It helps fix problems before someone gets hurt.

Example

Lerato sees a cracked rung on the ladder to the bin roof. She puts a do not use tag on it and tells her supervisor. The ladder is fixed the next day. Nobody falls.

Key points

  • Know the hazards in your workplace.
  • Obey safety signs and always wear your PPE.
  • Never remove guards or reach into running machines.
  • Lift with your legs and keep the workplace clean.
  • Keep waste, oil and chemicals out of water and the veld.
  • Report injuries, near misses and unsafe conditions at once.
